messages:
alex: Rolling traffic out of us-east-1 to us-west-2 — GPU pool in us-east is flapping and we’re hitting OOMs on infer-worker nodes. Starting DNS-based failover now. Current public A TTL=300, hoping to reduce window. Observing weird resolver behavior from some ISPs.

tara: lowering TTL to 60 via Cloud DNS now. will wait for txn commit then update records. note: lowering doesn't yank cached answers everywhere immediately.

jim: heads up — CDN edges (CloudFront / Fastly) can return cached origin IPs even after TTL change because of stale-if-error and negative cache. we should purge edges after the record flip.

maria: running dig checks from a few vantage points. some still return old IPs from ns1, ns2. pasting quick dig outputs:
```
; dig @8.8.8.8 A api.redwood.ai +short
34.82.10.11
```
and
```
; dig @1.1.1.1 A api.redwood.ai +short
35.201.22.9
```
(old vs new)

sre-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: route-shift started (incident-1794201123). Autoscale for us-west-2 enabled.

alex: doing the Cloud DNS transaction now:
```
gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-prod
gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name="api.redwood.ai." --ttl=300 --type=A 34.82.10.11 --zone=redwood-prod
gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name="api.redwood.ai." --ttl=60 --type=A 35.201.22.9 --zone=redwood-prod
gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-prod
```
commit done at 14:25 UTC.

tara: tx executed. also purging CloudFront invalidation for /v1/* and /health to force new IPs at edge. submitted invalidation id: I2K3X.

jim: after purge I'm still seeing dig results with the old IP from an ISP resolver in EU (~AT). this smells like recursive resolver caching or negative caching. check SOA serial and TTL at authoritative nameserver.

maria: grabbed authoritative response:
```
; dig @ns1.redwood-dns.net api.redwood.ai SOA +short
ns1.redwood-dns.net hostmaster.redwood-infra 2026031801 7200 3600 1209600 60
```
serial bumped. authoritative TTL is 60 now.

alex: run `curl -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" http://<ip>/health` against both IPs. us-west-2 responder OK (200), old us-east ip 502/timeout from some probes. suggests partial clients still hitting stale answer.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026.03.18-rollback-check succeeded. canary traffic moved to us-west-2.

jim: operational note — some consumer ISPs ignore low TTLs & respect their own min TTL (eg. 300/600). also EDNS0/DO flags can change caching behavior for DNSSEC; if resolvers saw a DNSSEC mismatch earlier they may negative-cache. unlikely but check negative TTLs.

tara: I opened a ticket with our DNS provider about resolver variants and asked them to push expedited propagation to major roots for our zone. they suggested increasing SOA refresh and monitoring.

maria: for verification, here's multi-region dig after invalidation:
```
// us-east probe
8.8.8.8 -> 34.82.10.11 (old)
// europe probe
1.1.1.1 -> 35.201.22.9 (new)
// apac probe
9.9.9.9 -> 35.201.22.9 (new)
```
we still have split-brain for ~10-12 minutes.

alex: mitigation checklist we used: lowered TTL, updated authoritative record, purged CDN, enabled autoscale in target region, monitored backends. fallback: manual BGP announcement if DNS propagation unacceptable.

jim: cost note — long-term plan: keep a pre-warmed small GPU pool in a secondary region (~10% baseline) to avoid emergency DNS flips that force expensive burst capacity. monthly cost delta estimate: ~$6k.

tara: postmortem action items: 1) set planned-failover TTL to 60 for zones before maintenance windows; 2) automate CDN purge after DNS flip; 3) add synthetic probes to detect stale answers per resolver family; 4) docs for runbook: when to consider BGP vs DNS.

alex: thanks all — we'll keep the incident open until global resolvers converge and error rates on client side drop below 1%. tagging for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
